description.from:
Purpose
Design and then implement a safe, authenticated recovery path for an individual legitimate email submission that fails automatic SES sender authentication, without weakening automatic acceptance. The first DreamHost-sent attempt from a test sender reached the receiver and was rejected with sender_authentication_failed; this is evidence of a strict-gate rejection, not proof of a broken sender configuration. Do not change trust policy or release either test message as part of this issue filing.

Verified current behavior and reuse
- src/papyrus_content/email_submission_intake.py::_trusted_envelope accepts only SES-invoked records with spam PASS, virus PASS, DMARC PASS, and SPF or DKIM PASS. The failed gate returns sender_authentication_failed before parsing the MIME or checking editor membership.
- The receiver already writes a receipt keyed by EMAIL#<hash>, keeps the original MIME in the private S3 email-submissions/ prefix for 30 days, and records normalized rejection status/errorCode. It currently does not persist per-verdict SES statuses/reasons or expose rejected receipts to editors.
- Use the receipt and existing private object as the quarantine source; do not copy raw mail into another bucket or make S3 public. Reuse the newsroom authenticated API/authorizer and the per-publication current verified-editor/admin membership checks used by email intake. Reuse the established editor moderation-panel pattern for a small quarantine/recovery view; reader-moderation records are not themselves email quarantine.
- A manual release should re-enter the existing bounded, idempotent email intake / Monitoring discovery / Reference pipeline for only the authorized publication(s). Do not invoke Cyclotron, training, section labels, publish, or execute instructions during release.

Design and acceptance requirements
1. Keep the automatic SES gate unchanged. Persist only a bounded normalized record of each SES receipt verdict (spam, virus, SPF, DKIM, DMARC: exact SES status and a bounded reason/code only when SES supplies one). Explicitly represent unavailable reason as unavailable. Keep SES event verdicts distinct from Authentication-Results in the untrusted MIME headers; never treat a MIME header as authoritative evidence. Exclude raw event, IPs, tokens, message body, and unbounded diagnostics from the receipt.
2. Quarantine only an exact configured recipient and an authentication-only rejection eligible for safe review. Spam/virus FAIL or unavailable, recipient-scope mismatch, malformed/oversized mail, and unsafe/unparseable content must not be editor-releasable. Fail closed if receipt-to-publication binding or current membership cannot be resolved.
3. Add an editor-visible queue scoped to publication/account. Only an authenticated enabled editor/admin currently authorized for that publication can inspect a receipt or release it. Shared-destination access must be restricted per publication; membership on one child publication cannot grant access to another. Never expose raw S3 access to the browser.
4. Render a safe preview only: sanitized text, no active HTML/scripts/forms/remote images, no automatic URL fetches, and redact recipient-specific tracking/action URLs and unsubscribe/account/login links. Make sender, timestamp, recipient scope, processing stage and each SES verdict/reason understandable; do not show raw headers or credentials.
5. Require a deliberate per-message release action. Record an append-only audit event with actor, timestamp, receipt, publication binding, normalized verdict snapshot, action, idempotency key and outcome. Use a conditional state transition so concurrent/double clicks or retried requests cannot create duplicate discoveries. Deactivation/revocation takes effect on the release request; fail closed on lookup failure. Release is a one-message override, not sender enrollment or a change to future trust.
6. Preserve original raw mail under the existing private 30-day lifecycle and apply a bounded retention to quarantine metadata/audit in line with it; expired items are no longer readable/releasable. Do not lengthen retention or keep a second raw copy by default.
7. Bound abuse/storage: deduplicate SES message IDs, enforce bounded per-recipient quarantine volume/rate and request/read limits without using untrusted From as authenticated identity, and make overflow/rejection visible. Do not create a user-enumeration oracle.
8. Show precise states: quarantined, released/queued, expired, ineligible, and retryable dependency failure. Preserve per-gate status and safe reason codes in operational diagnostics. No silent loss; no human label or publication occurs.
9. Cover Gherkin and unit/integration tests: auth-only DKIM/DMARC failure is reviewable but not auto-accepted; spam/virus failure and unknown recipient are not releasable; cross-publication editor denial; disabled/revoked editor denial; safe rendering; expired retention; conditional concurrent release; duplicate retries; audit record; downstream intake remains idempotent; SES verdicts are not confused with spoofable MIME Authentication-Results.

Permission and review boundary
This issue records a reviewed design before implementation. It does not authorize production deployment, new IAM/persistent access, SES/DNS/rule changes, email sends, retroactive release of either existing test message, or changes to automatic SES trust. Before coding any auth-sensitive release endpoint/UI or new storage/index/IAM, present the concrete data-flow, exact resource/permission scope, retention and abuse controls for review. Preserve the current no-deploy hold on PR #667; keep this recovery design/code in separate work.
